contents.entry: Mechanism: Inbox.Message, the rule table, the ack ladder, Inbox.Reply
The ack ladder the owner sees
How it starts without an agent typing
Every wait, its timeout and its fallback
State paths and their cleanup scripts
The look of a bubble and its receipts

pointers.sibling: JSON schema of owner.message, routed.message, ack and reply
Bearings page service: the message leaves the page here and the acks go back to it
Watcher: the second deliverer of every message
Ticket intake: a message the rule turns into a ticket request
Owner answer intake: USERHALT and USERGO route here as control actions
Phone push bridge ships dark until this node is live
pointers.shared: Owner words: the whole trimmed message from an owner principal
Where this node goes live in the one cut-over order of the book

purpose.is: The inbox takes every message the owner types on the page, persists it, routes it by rule to one lane and one consumer, and sends the owner a receipt at each step: accepted, routed, consumed, answered, or stale when a step is late.
purpose.is-not: It is not a chat with an LLM, never prompts an agent per message, and never decides what the owner meant beyond the rule table.
purpose.why: Every owner message landed in the architect's context as a prompt ("having every message to you instead of some kind of board is fucking you up", 2026-10-13), delivery was marked consumed before the prompt was sent (L08 finding 6), and the owner said on 2026-10-14 that our comms suck (m-20261014033542616-u5bl9). The ruling on C58: a Go inbox with acks over the push stream; a phone push channel bridged afterwards.
purpose.decisions: C58 comms, D12 system lane (C40), D21 push (C52), V13 the doorbell is not the mail (a nudge carries a lane and a count, the worker pulls), K01 no LLM in the dispatch path, K03 no agent polls, STD-owner-comms-001 for every reply.

owner or viewer, the role of the page session that sent it (nodes/N-32/spec.xml#web-security); only an owner message can carry an owner word
true only for the legacy messages of the cut-over import; an imported message is never routed
8000 chars max (config max_message_chars)
0 to 8 attachment ids stored by N-32
an optional message id or card id the owner is answering under

input.text: The record arrives by gRPC Inbox.Message from the page service in the same request as the owner's send, and a second time from the watcher (N-27) by stream. Both are the same record id.

record.field: the message id
control, ticket, card, sitrep, architect, system or unroutable

the node or role that must act: N-29 for control, N-03 for ticket, N-29 for card (as a relay-free answer thread), the SITREP builder for sitrep, the digest builder (code inside N-30, step 3) for architect, N-06 for system
the rule id that matched
the lane's consume bound from the rule table
the message id
accepted (100), routed (100), consumed (100), deferred (100), answered (200), stale (500)
who produced the state: inbox, the consumer's lease holder, the replier
the routed.message, lease or reply record id behind the state
the message id the reply answers (the same field name event.sh uses for an answer to a request)
plain text, 32000 chars max, or a #SITREP/v1# payload
the seat or node that replied
0 to 8 http(s) URLs, clickable on the page; never a key

output.text: Acks are upserts keyed ack:<message> whose state only moves forward (accepted, routed, consumed, deferred, answered; stale is a side state that clears to consumed or answered; deferred means the system sent a templated holding line in place of the reader and a real reply is still owed, and it clears to answered only when a reply names the message). The page draws the latest state as the receipt mark on the bubble. The reply is pushed to the page as the agent's bubble, where the old reply.mjs appended to messages.jsonl.

mechanism.where: Go service (D01), package internal/owner/inbox, gRPC service Inbox with Message(MessageRequest), Reply(ReplyRequest) and Ack(AckRequest) on the control socket. Rule table in the repository at tools/bearings/config/inbox-rules.json, validated by its schema at make lint, loaded with Reload (N-43 shape).
mechanism.step: Persist owner.message (operation key N-30/owner.message/<id>/r1; a repeat replays the stored record and its current ack). Write ack accepted 100 in the same transaction. An imported message (imported true) is stored with ack answered reason imported in the same commit and stops here: it is never routed, never matched as an owner word and never turned into an effect (shared/authority.xml#relayable-rulings). Reply to the caller with the ack, so the page can draw the first receipt before anything else runs. Durable then acknowledged (bearings-v2 requirement, L08 section 8).

Route: first the owner-word test (shared/authority.xml#owner-words): the text with leading and trailing white space removed equals GOFACTORY, USERGO or USERHALT exactly, and principal_role is owner; a match is R01 to R03 and nothing else is tried. A message that contains a word but is not the word alone ("don't GOFACTORY yet", a quote) is an ordinary message and gets one templated reply that an owner word is sent alone. Then evaluate the rule table top to bottom on the message (prefix, keyword, reply_to kind, attachment presence); the first match gives lane, consumer, sla and an optional transform (a ticket request body, a control action). Write routed.message 300 and ack routed 100. No match is lane unroutable with consumer architect and a system alert inbox.unroutable 500, so a message is never dropped and the gap is a rule ticket.

Deliver: the consumer is a node or a lane. A node consumer (N-29 for control and card, N-03 for ticket, N-06 for system, the SITREP builder for sitrep) is called by gRPC with the fencing token of the inbox's own lease; the node's acceptance writes ack consumed 100 with ref the node's record. The architect lane's consumer is code too, the digest builder (package internal/owner/inbox/digest): it appends the message to the open digest as digest.item 100 (keyed by message id, the referenced record attached for R08) and writes ack consumed at once, so no seat has to exist for the lane to move. The digest (SPEC-17 s-architect shape: one batched read every 30 minutes, a p0 at once, never a prompt per record) is read by the owner's architect session through coq inbox digest --since, under the owner's host CLI identity (shared/seat-contract.xml#relay), never pushed into a prompt; a reply through Inbox.Reply naming the message writes ack answered. When no reply names the message within the lane's sla (1800 s), the builder replies itself with a templated holding line (still in the architect digest; prefix cut: to make it work, or answer the card) and writes ack deferred with reason digest-timeout: the owner sees the system has it and a reader is owed, never a false answered; a later reply naming the message moves the ack to answered, and a deferred item with no reply after a further 24 h is one digest p0 line, never a card.

Answer: a reply record naming the message (Inbox.Reply, answer=message id) writes ack answered 200 and is pushed to the page. For a control message the ruling from N-29 is the answer and its text is templated (halt done at, resume done at); a control.refused 412 not-ready from N-29 is answered with its missing proofs. For a ticket request the accepted ticket record (N-18 validator) is the answer and its text names the ticket id with its full title.

Stale: the stall tick (N-12 clock) scans acks every 10 s; a routed with no consumed past sla_seconds, or a consumed with no answered past 2 times sla, writes ack stale 500 and an alert message.stale 500 to N-41. The owner sees STALE on his bubble, which is the honest state, and the system (not the owner) chases: the consumer's lease is checked, a dead consumer is restarted by its node's own rule, and a second stale on one message is an owner-acts code (N-28 cards it: "your message from 09:14 has no reader; drop it or hold it").

Inbox.Reply runs the comms checker (internal/owner/commscheck: bubble is at most two sentences of 15 words or fewer, no semicolon, ticket ids with full titles, no key, no em dash; a SITREP payload goes through the sitrep rules) and refuses with reply.refused 400 to the sender; a refused reply never reaches the owner and the seat's result carries the violation so a fresh seat fixes it (D02 one-shot seats).
mechanism.text: Why four acks and not one: the owner's complaint is not latency (median 32 s) but not knowing whether anyone has it. Accepted says the system has it; routed says where it went; consumed says a reader took it; answered says it is done; stale says the system knows it is late. Each is a record, so the health line counts them and nothing is an opinion.

Why the architect is a digest lane and never a prompt target: K01 and the 2026-10-13 flood; the architect's own rule (memory architect-queue-clear-by-listed-id) and SPEC-17 s-architect agree on one batched pull. A message that needs the architect waits for the digest, and the owner sees routed with the lane name, which is the truth.

rule.match: trimmed text is exactly USERHALT and principal_role is owner

rules.rule: transform: owner.answer on the standing halt card (nodes/N-28/spec.xml#standing-cards) with source=page, via=message, action_id=the message id; N-29 rules control.halt and N-44 sets flag:hold; reply templated with the halt record time

rule.match: trimmed text is exactly USERGO and principal_role is owner

rules.rule: transform: owner.answer on the standing resume card, same form; before bootstrap B7 N-29 answers control.refused 412 not-ready naming the missing proofs (shared/cut-over.xml#bootstrap) and the reply names them; at B7 the ruling is the go-live, after B8 it clears a hold

rule.match: trimmed text is exactly GOFACTORY and principal_role is owner

rules.rule: transform: owner.answer on the standing GOFACTORY card, same form; one time (a second gofactory effect is a no-op at N-49 and N-50)

transform: words appended to the card thread; if the card is open, is not owner-only, and the text names an option label exactly, it is an owner.answer with source=page, via=tap; otherwise a thread note the page shows under the card (an owner-only card is answered only by its option tap or, for the standing cards, its owner word)
transform: ticket.request with the text as the brief; one ticket request per message id (dag.md re-entry bound); the validator's acceptance or refusal is the answer
the SITREP builder renders from records (tools/bearings/scripts/sitrep-build.mjs carried into Go) and replies with a #SITREP/v1# payload; no agent writes it
a health question; the reply is the health line in prose, templated

rule.match: text contains a URL to a PR or a ticket id

rules.rule: appended to the digest with the referenced record attached; consumed at once; answered by a reply; deferred by the builder's templated holding line at the sla

the default; routed with the lane shown; consumed at once by the digest builder; answered by a reply, deferred by the builder's templated holding line at the sla, so the owner's bubble never goes stale for want of a reader and never reads answered when nobody answered
rules.text: A viewer session, a relayed text, an imported message or any text an agent produced never matches R01 to R03 (shared/authority.xml#owner-words); text that merely contains a word is never one.

The table is data; a rule change is a pull request with make lint running every rule against the fixtures in tools/bearings/tests/inbox/. The owner may address a lane explicitly with a prefix (control:, ticket:, sitrep:, system:, arch:), which wins over keyword matching, so the rule is the owner's and the keyword is only a convenience.

state.name: accepted
state.shows: one tick mark on the bubble

state.name: routed
state.shows: two tick marks and the lane name

state.name: consumed
state.when: the consumer's record or lease claim exists

state.name: deferred
state.when: the digest builder sent its templated holding line at the sla
state.shows: a held mark: the system has it, a reader owes a reply
state.bound: cleared to answered by a reply; a further 24 h is a digest p0 line

state.name: answered
state.when: a reply or the consumer's result names the message

state.name: stale
state.shows: STALE in heat-bar red with the elapsed time
state.bound: cleared by the next forward state

start.text: Inbox is a gRPC service inside coq.service (N-06 unit.start). It ships dark behind inbox.enabled and goes live by its own ticket with the proof: a message on dev shows accepted, routed and consumed receipts within the bounds, a USERHALT on dev produces a control ruling, a reply through Inbox.Reply draws on the page and a 16-word reply is refused. While dark, the old reply.mjs path and the wait loop stay on stable; the cut-over step in N-32's runbook retires them.

wait.fallback: retry 3 times (1, 2, 4 s) then inbox.unavailable 503 to the caller; the page keeps the message queued with a 'not sent' mark and retries; the watcher's stream is the second path
R99 default with an alert rule.timeout 500; a slow rule is a defect ticket

retry 3 times (1, 2, 4 s) then ack stays routed and the stall scan writes stale at sla; the level-triggered scan retries delivery every 10 s until consumed, bounded by the owner-acts card after the second stale

wait.what: a reply to a digest item (architect lane)
wait.fallback: the digest builder replies with the templated holding line and writes ack deferred reason digest-timeout; the item stays in the digest for the architect session; no stale, no card, never a false answered
retry 3 times; then reply.failed 500 returned to the sender, whose seat result carries it; the owner's ack stays consumed, never a false answered
keep the last good table; alert

waits.no-cog: The cog that could stall this node is a consumer that never reads (the old architect). Every lane's consumer is now code (the architect lane's is the digest builder), so a message is always consumed; the lane's sla bounds the answer, with the templated reply for the architect lane and the stale receipt plus one card after the second stale for a node consumer that fails. The inbox never waits on a human to accept a message.

retries.rule: Every store and gRPC call retries 3 times with backoff then writes a 500 or 503 and continues; the stall scan every 10 s is the recovery for any delivery that was dropped, and it is idempotent because every ack is an upsert keyed on the message id whose state only moves forward.
A message is never marked consumed before a consumer's record exists (the fix for L08 finding 6).

many-agents-at-once.readers: Any number of seats read this volume; the rule table is one file, one ticket at a time, with fixtures.
many-agents-at-once.workers: Build tickets touch internal/owner/inbox, internal/owner/commscheck, internal/owner/sitrep, the Inbox proto service, tools/bearings/config/inbox-rules.json and tools/bearings/tests/inbox/; other G5 nodes own other files.

collision.what: the page service and the watcher both deliver one message

many-agents-at-once.collision: Same id: persist is a no-op and the ack is returned; the rule is not re-evaluated when routed.message exists (operation key N-30/route/<message id>/r1).

collision.what: two seats reply to one message

many-agents-at-once.collision: Both replies are stored and pushed in seq order; answered is set by the first; the second is a further bubble. Nothing is lost, and the owner sees two voices, which is the truth; the digest rule says the architect replies once per item, enforced by the seat contract, not by dropping a reply.

collision.what: two consumers claim one digest item

many-agents-at-once.collision: The lane item is leased (N-02) by the first claim; the second gets lease.refused and moves on; the ack consumed names the holder.

collision.what: a reply arrives before the message is routed (a seat answering from the push stream)

many-agents-at-once.collision: The reply names the message; answered is set; the route step still runs for the record but the ack ladder does not move backwards. The consumer is told the message is already answered by the reply's existence (level-triggered), so it skips.

collision.what: ack upserts from the inbox and from the stall scan at once

many-agents-at-once.collision: Compare-and-swap on version; the loser re-reads and applies only a forward move; stale never overwrites answered.
many-agents-at-once.test: tests run two Inbox clients, a fake consumer that sometimes times out, and the stall scan under the fake clock: every message reaches answered or stale within its bounds, no ack moves backwards, no message is consumed without a consumer record, a 16-word reply is refused.

look.rule: The owner's bubble and the receipt marks follow the Factorio GUI values: the bubble in inside_shallow_frame #403F40 on the page's deep frame #242324, receipt tick marks in production green #2BE327 as they advance, the lane name in the caption colour #FFE6C0 at default-small size, STALE in heat-bar red #DA4535 with the elapsed time in count-font, the agent reply bubble in the inset #313031 with links in blue #80CEF0. A SITREP payload draws as the existing coloured status panel re-skinned to the same values. Font Titillium Web. No Wube or BiusArt pixel.
look.check: Playwright on dev asserts the five receipt states' colours and the lane label text; screenshots of a message walking the ladder go to the owner before the uat confirm card.

permissions.runs-as: inside coq-service as the service user coq-svc (shared/authority.xml#principals); Inbox is served on /run/coq/store.sock
permissions.callers: Message: the page service (passing the session's role) and the watcher (second delivery of a stored record) only. Reply: system nodes, and the owner's architect session through the owner CLI (the digest reader); seats have no socket and their reply rides their result. Ack: consumer nodes only. Every caller is judged by SO_PEERCRED (shared/authority.xml#role-derivation), never by COQ_SEAT.
permissions.may-not: no seat may call Message (a seat never speaks as the owner); no pod reaches the socket; no reply may carry a page key (the checker refuses the key pattern)

counter.name: replies_refused_total

histogram.on: N-40; the comms latency the owner can read

runbook.op: coq owner reply --to 20261014T033542Z-100-u5bl9 "text" (the CLI calls Inbox.Reply and prints the ack or the violations); a seat never calls it (no socket): a seat's words reach the page only through its result, which the node that reads the result replies with
coq owner inbox --tier stable --open (messages not yet answered with their ack state and lane)
edit tools/bearings/config/inbox-rules.json and a fixture, make lint, pull request; coq reload
read its routed lane; the fix is the consumer's node runbook, never a hand reply that pretends it was read
coq owner import-messages --file ~/.bearings/coq-stable/messages.jsonl --dry-run, then --yes (every line imported true, ack answered reason imported, never routed)
store retention by N-45; journal by tools/bearings/bin/cleanup-journal.sh; legacy by tools/bearings/bin/cleanup-tier.sh --legacy
runbook.cost: A rule table to maintain; the architect reads the owner's general messages only every digest interval, which the owner sees on the receipt; four small writes per message.
